title: inference-task-tickets-land-in-the-logs-tree
intention: The inference domain's task tickets (one JSON per inference call) land under the logs tree at address.log_path('inference_domain', 0)/tickets, i.e. ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/tickets/, instead of the device's state directory ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/tickets/; domain.tickets_dir() answers the new address (still following set_diagnostic_roots), the tickets already written move there once, and read_task_tickets and the completeness probe read them from there.
why: Akien answered open-5ec505c169c1: inference task tickets are logging artifacts and belong in the logs tree (30-day trail for relearning and forensics); today they sit in the device's state directory, grow ~280/day, and push every proof sandbox past its 150MB bound, so the tester component stays red.
traces_to: Law 5 (the address carries what a mind needs now; a logging artifact is not the device's state); Law 6 (logs/ is one machine-scoped root, so the 30-day deletion crosses nobody's gate); ticket 1c4ae8f053fe (the per-proof sandbox bound); the three retention classes (test runs and logging: 30 days, disposable).
how: Akien, verbatim (open-5ec505c169c1): 'they are a logging artifact, so the intention is that they wind up in the logging tree. their consumers are: learning loops. if we make a change to our learning, we don't have to rerun the inference calls, we can relearn off the same data. second, if we discover an issue, we have the complete history of inference for the last 30 days, a complete log trail for each call. Forensic levels of information ... It's already worked 3 times in that role.' Measured 2026-10-02: ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/tickets holds 2048 files, 73MB (1386 files, 49MB on 2026-10-01), oldest 2026-09-17; test_isolation reds at 182MB against ticket 1c4ae8f053fe's 150MB per-proof sandbox bound, and this folder is the largest grower. Every reader goes through domain.tickets_dir (cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py:222): _ticket_path, read_task_tickets, the probe are_inference_task_tickets_complete. address.log_path (cairn/tools/base/address.py:148) is the logs-tree address, whose why is retention ('easy to delete everything in the logs tree over 30 days old in one go', Akien 2026-08-18), and snapshot_instance_space already empties the instance root's logs/ (cairn/devices/tester/isolation.py:273-281). So: tickets_dir returns address.log_path('inference_domain', 0, table) / TICKETS; the existing files are moved once with the build (mv, not copy: a ticket has one address); the probe's docstring names the new address; long-running devices that import the domain are restarted so no stale process writes to the old address. The 30-day sweep of the logs tree itself is not this ticket's: no sweep exists in code (measured: no mtime-age deletion anywhere under cairn/), and it is cast as its own ticket.
falsifier: RED if: (1) domain.tickets_dir() with no roots table does not equal address.log_path('inference_domain', 0) / 'tickets', or it lies under address.instance_path('inference_domain', 0); (2) under a temp roots table, a ticket written through domain._write_task_ticket does not land under that table's logs tree, or read_task_tickets with that table does not read it back; (3) the live ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/tickets holds any .json file. WRONG INTENT if a consumer needs a task ticket kept past 30 days. Horizon: the tester seal of cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_task_tickets_land_in_the_logs_tree.py.
watchme: none, because the sandbox bound in cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_isolation.py reds if anything heavy grows outside logs/ again, and tooth 3 of this ticket's proof reads the live old address at every reseal
children: none, because the 30-day sweep of the logs tree is a sibling cast as its own ticket, not a part of this move
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Where? cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py:222, tickets_dir returns address.log_path('inference_domain', 0, table) / TICKETS; docstring names the logs tree and why. (2) The existing files? mkdir -p ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/tickets and mv the old folder's *.json there, then rmdir the old folder. (3) Proof? cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_task_tickets_land_in_the_logs_tree.py, PROVES keys 1-4, red first.

chart_claim.filled_by: CC chart chain (orient ea54e0730230 .. validate 4b7697d27ab1, each learned)

decisions.text: D1 ADDRESS: in cairn/devices/inference_domain/domain.py, tickets_dir(roots) returns address.log_path('inference_domain', 0, table) / TICKETS. TICKETS is the existing module constant (domain.py:215, TICKETS = "tickets"), used as-is. table is the same `roots if roots is not None else getattr(_trail, '_diagnostic_roots', None)` it computes today. Its docstring says the tickets are a LOGGING artifact (Akien, open-5ec505c169c1: learning loops relearn off them, forensics read the 30-day trail), so they live under <instance>/logs/inference_domain/0/tickets. Nothing else in domain.py changes.

D2 THE PROBE: the docstring of cairn/devices/inference_domain/probes/are_inference_task_tickets_complete.py names the address as ``logs/inference_domain/0/tickets/`` (in the logs tree, ticket 07f415c15970) instead of ``devices/inference_domain/0/tickets/``. Its code reads through domain.read_task_tickets and is unchanged.

D3 THE SIBLING PROOF: in cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_task_ticket.py, the file exists and spells the old temp address tmp / 'devices' / 'inference_domain' / '0' / 'tickets' in exactly two places, the _tickets(tmp) helper and one assertion that globs the tickets folder directly (grep -n "'devices'" finds both); both read tmp / 'logs' / 'inference_domain' / '0' / 'tickets'. Nothing else changes; it runs green bare.

D4 THE MOVE — ALREADY DONE, and recorded here as what was done, not as work left. D1-D3 were committed first as build commit 1bdf534c (subject '07f415c15970: build — inference task tickets land in the logs tree'); then CC ran, once: (1) `systemctl --user stop cairn-ground-loop.service` (the in-process ticket writer); (2) `mkdir -p ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/tickets`; (3) `find ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/tickets -maxdepth 1 -name '*.json' -exec mv -n -t ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/tickets {} +` (mv -n never overwrites); (4) the emptied old folder goes to the trash with `bin/cmd/trash ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/tickets` (the deletegate refuses rmdir under ~/.cairn); (5) restart through the same call every shim makes, repeated until it prints spawned 'unit' (it spawns nothing until the stopped loop's liveness record is older than 300 s): `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c 'from datetime import datetime; from cairn.tools.base.shim import ensure_ground_loop; print(ensure_ground_loop(datetime.now().astimezone()))'`; (6) after two 60 s beats, counted both folders. Nothing in this step is repeated by anyone.

D5 THE PROOF — ALREADY WRITTEN AND COMMITTED (last at d7f6f152, by CC); the builder writes no test code. It is cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_task_tickets_land_in_the_logs_tree.py with exactly three teeth, PROVES {'07f415c15970': {'1': 'tickets_dir_is_the_logs_tree_address', '2': 'a_written_ticket_lands_in_the_logs_tree_and_reads_back', '3': 'the_old_address_holds_no_ticket'}}, matching falsifier clauses 1-3. The cast's fourth tooth (the live new folder holds tickets) is not in it: every proof sandbox empties logs/, so that tooth reads red under the seal by construction, and a tooth that skipped itself under the seal would be a hollow green. Its docstring says so in a paragraph headed 'NO TOOTH FOR "THE TICKETS MOVED"'. The builder runs it bare and reads 3 passed.

D6 THE MEASUREMENT OF THE MOVE — ALREADY WRITTEN AND COMMITTED at 45c854e6, by CC; nothing remains to do here. It went in the device's history instead of a tooth: one entry appended to cairn/devices/inference_domain/history.json by these steps: read the existing history.json (a JSON array), append the entry below as its last element, json.dump the whole array to a file in the builder's session scratchpad directory (the directory the session names for temporary files, never the repo), and pass that file to `cairn artifact write <abs path> --verb append --why '<why>' --from <that file>`. The numbers in it are the ones CC measured while doing D4, copied as measured; no one substitutes or re-measures them. The entry, as it stands in the file: {"seq": 47, "at": "2026-10-02T11:10:00-06:00", "act": "measured", "actor": "CC", "ticket": "07f415c15970", "standing": "BUILDME", "why": "THE MOVE, measured once at the build (decisions D4, D6): the ground loop (cairn-ground-loop.service, pid 126256, writer of 827 of the tickets) was stopped; 2058 task tickets moved with mv -n from ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/tickets to ~/.cairn/logs/inference_domain/0/tickets; 0 were left at the old address, and the empty folder went to the trash (bin/cmd/trash). The loop came back through ensure_ground_loop (spawned 'unit' once liveness passed its 300s threshold), and two beats later the new folder held 2066 tickets and the old address none. Not a standing tooth: every proof sandbox empties logs/, which is why they moved there."}
